source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is a client usually taught to use transdermal nitroglycerin patches?
options: A new patch once every 7 days
A new patch each morning, off at night
One patch worn for 3 days straight
A patch only during chest pain
questions.rationale: A new patch is applied each morning and left on for 12 to 16 hours as prescribed. The patch-free period helps prevent tolerance. Daily application ensures proper dosing.
explanations: Correct: a daily patch with a patch-free period.
Patches are not used for acute pain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1251 (PDF p. 1550)
questions.quote: The client is generally advised to apply a new medication patch each morning and leave it in place for 12 to 16 hours

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client admitted after fainting is on olanzapine. For which condition is this drug most likely prescribed?
questions.rationale: Olanzapine is an atypical antipsychotic and a first-line treatment for schizophrenia, targeting positive and negative symptoms. It can cause orthostatic hypotension, so clients rise slowly.
explanations: Correct: an atypical antipsychotic for schizophrenia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1260 (PDF p. 1561)
questions.quote: It is the first-line treatment for schizophrenia, targeting both the positive and the negative symptoms.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client receives NPH insulin at 7 AM. During which period is hypoglycemia MOST likely?
options: 11 AM to 7 PM, 4 to 12 hours after
questions.rationale: NPH is an intermediate-acting insulin that peaks 4 to 12 hours after it is given, when hypoglycemia is most likely.
explanations: This is closer to the peak of short-acting insulin.
Correct: the NPH peak is 4 to 12 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1264 (PDF p. 1565)
questions.quote: NPH is an intermediate-acting insulin with a peak time in 4 to 12 hours.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding in a client on haloperidol is an ADVERSE effect that should be reported?
questions.rationale: Antipsychotic adverse effects include extrapyramidal symptoms such as parkinsonism (drooling), dystonia, akathisia, and tardive dyskinesia. Nausea, hypotension, and blurred vision are occasional side effects.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1265 (PDF p. 1566)
questions.quote: extrapyramidal symptoms, including parkinsonism effects (drooling)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with acute gouty arthritis is prescribed indomethacin. Which statement shows the client needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll rest when my joint is painful.'
'I'll call if I notice a rash.'
'I'll take a pill only when the pain is bad.'
questions.rationale: Indomethacin is given on a schedule, not as needed. Rest relieves gout pain, a rash may mean hypersensitivity, and gastric distress or swelling is reported.
explanations: Correct answer: it is taken on schedule, not PRN.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1266 (PDF p. 1567)
questions.quote: Indomethacin may alleviate pain but is administered on a scheduled time frame, not on an as-needed schedule.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is on a continuous IV heparin infusion. Which finding should the nurse watch for as an adverse effect?
questions.rationale: Heparin increases the risk of bleeding: gum bleeding, ecchymoses, pink or cloudy urine, tarry stools, and occult blood in body fluids.
explanations: Not a direct effect of heparin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1277 (PDF p. 1576)
questions.quote: The nurse monitors for signs of bleeding, which includes bleeding from the gums, ecchymoses on the skin

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chemical cardioversion is ordered for a client with atrial fibrillation. Which drug does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Amiodarone, an antidysrhythmic, can restore normal sinus rhythm in atrial fibrillation. Lidocaine treats ventricular dysrhythmias. Continuous cardiac monitoring is required.
explanations: A vasodilator, not used for cardioversion.
A vasodilator, not used for cardioversion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1279 (PDF p. 1580)
questions.quote: Amiodarone is an antidysrhythmic that is useful in restoring normal sinus rhythm for the client experiencing atrial fibrillation.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with ventricular dysrhythmia receives an IV bolus of lidocaine. What should the nurse monitor MOST closely?
questions.rationale: During an IV lidocaine bolus, the nurse monitors respiratory status and blood pressure. The apical pulse is preferred over the radial.
explanations: Correct: lidocaine can depress BP and breathing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1290 (PDF p. 1591)
questions.quote: The nurse is responsible for monitoring the client’s respiratory status and blood pressure while he or she is being treated with an IV bolus of this medication.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Addison's disease takes fludrocortisone. Which therapeutic effect should the nurse focus on?
questions.rationale: Fludrocortisone is a mineralocorticoid. It makes the kidneys reabsorb sodium and excrete potassium, restoring electrolyte and fluid balance and preventing hypotension.
explanations: Correct: it promotes sodium retention and potassium excretion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1311 (PDF p. 1613)
questions.quote: Mineralocorticoids act on the renal distal tubules to enhance the reabsorption of sodium and chloride ions and the excretion of potassium and hydrogen ions.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When should blood for a serum digoxin level be drawn?
questions.rationale: Digoxin levels are usually drawn just before a dose (or 6 to 8 hours after one) so the result is not falsely high.
explanations: Correct: a trough level avoids a false high.
The level would be falsely elevated.
The level would be falsely elevated.
The level would be falsely elevated.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1317 (PDF p. 1619)
questions.quote: Drawing the medication before a dose ensures that the level is not falsely elevated.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a client take aluminum hydroxide tablets?
questions.rationale: Aluminum hydroxide tablets are chewed thoroughly so they do not reach the small intestine undissolved. They are taken 2 hours apart from other drugs. Constipation is a side effect, but a laxative is not taken with every dose.
explanations: Antacids interact with other drugs; separate them by 2 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1320 (PDF p. 1622)
questions.quote: Aluminum hydroxide tablets should be chewed thoroughly before swallowing.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Prednisone is newly prescribed. Which drug on the client's record should the nurse discuss with the prescriber?
questions.rationale: Prednisone irritates the GI tract. Aspirin and NSAIDs add to this irritation and are avoided during corticosteroid therapy. Clients on prednisone are also watched for hyperglycemia and hypokalemia.
explanations: Correct: aspirin plus a steroid increases GI injury.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1334 (PDF p. 1636)
questions.quote: products such as aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) and nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs are not used during corticosteroid therapy.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with von Willebrand disease is prescribed intranasal desmopressin. Which instruction should the nurse give the parents?
options: Reduce fluid intake during early treatment
Keep the spray in the freezer
questions.rationale: Desmopressin reduces urine output, so fluids are reduced during initial treatment to prevent fluid buildup. The spray is refrigerated, not frozen.
explanations: Correct: limit fluids during early treatment.
Extra doses are not given without orders.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1342 (PDF p. 1645)
questions.quote: Parents should be instructed to reduce fluid intake during initial treatment

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with acute myocardial infarction is receiving alteplase. Which finding suggests a complication?
questions.rationale: Bleeding, superficial or internal, is the main adverse effect of thrombolytic therapy. A nosebleed is a sign of it.
explanations: Not a typical complication of alteplase.
Expected in MI; not a drug complication.
Not a typical complication of alteplase.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1357 (PDF p. 1660)
questions.quote: Bleeding is an adverse effect of altepase therapy.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Methylergonovine is given IM to a mother right after delivery. What is its purpose?
options: To maintain a normal blood pressure
questions.rationale: Methylergonovine is an oxytocic that contracts the uterus to prevent or control postpartum hemorrhage. It may raise blood pressure.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1363 (PDF p. 1666)
questions.quote: Methylergonovine maleate, an oxytocic, is an agent used to prevent or control postpartum hemorrhage by contracting the uterus.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A laboring client receives butorphanol for pain. Which item must be readily available?
questions.rationale: Butorphanol is an opioid analgesic. Naloxone and resuscitation equipment are kept ready in case of respiratory depression.
explanations: Another opioid; it would add to depression.
May be useful, but not the priority.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1365 (PDF p. 1668)
questions.quote: The nurse should ensure that naloxone and resuscitation equipment are readily available to treat respiratory depression

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client understands allopurinol therapy for gout?
options: 'I'll put ice on my lips if they swell.'
'I'll drink at least 8 glasses of fluid daily.'
'I'll stop it if I get a rash, then restart.'
questions.rationale: Clients on allopurinol drink about 3,000 mL of fluid daily. Rash, eye irritation, or lip swelling may mean hypersensitivity and is reported. The drug is taken with or right after meals.
explanations: It is taken with or after meals.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1367 (PDF p. 1670)
questions.quote: Clients taking allopurinol are encouraged to drink 3000 mL of fluid a day.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A mother receives the rubella vaccine 2 days after delivery. Which instruction is MOST important?
options: Stay out of the sun for 3 days
questions.rationale: Rubella vaccine is a live attenuated virus that can harm a developing fetus, so the woman avoids pregnancy for the period advised after vaccination. Immunity lasts about 15 years.
explanations: Correct: the live vaccine is potentially teratogenic.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1368 (PDF p. 1671)
questions.quote: Because rubella is a live vaccine, it will act as the virus and is potentially teratogenic

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on phenelzine suddenly has a severe occipital headache, stiff neck, sweating, and very high BP. Which drug should the nurse prepare?
questions.rationale: These are signs of an MAOI hypertensive crisis. Phentolamine given IV is the antidote.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1375 (PDF p. 1678)
questions.quote: The antidote for hypertensive crisis is phentolamine

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with CKD is receiving epoetin alfa. Which serious adverse effect should the nurse monitor for?
questions.rationale: Hypertension and seizures are the most serious adverse effects of epoetin alfa. The drug treats anemia.
explanations: Not an adverse effect of epoetin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1384 (PDF p. 1687)
questions.quote: The client taking epoetin alfa is at risk of hypertension and seizure activity as the most serious adverse effects of therapy.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is on lansoprazole. Which pain reliever is the SAFEST choice?
questions.rationale: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome causes gastric hypersecretion. Aspirin and NSAIDs irritate the stomach lining, so acetaminophen is used for pain.
explanations: An NSAID that irritates the stomach.
An NSAID that irritates the stomach.
Correct: does not irritate the gastric lining.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1385 (PDF p. 1688)
questions.quote: The client should take acetaminophen for pain relief.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should a client take amiloride 10 mg daily for hypertension?
options: At bedtime on an empty stomach
Only when the BP is high
questions.rationale: Amiloride, a potassium-sparing diuretic, is taken in the morning to avoid nocturia and with food to improve bioavailability. Sodium is restricted when it is used for hypertension.
explanations: It is taken daily, not as needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1388 (PDF p. 1691)
questions.quote: A daily dose should be taken in the morning to avoid nocturia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is diphenhydramine given to a client before a blood transfusion?
questions.rationale: Urticaria (rash with itching) is a transfusion reaction that premedication with an antihistamine can prevent. Acetaminophen is given to prevent fever and chills.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1390 (PDF p. 1693)
questions.quote: Urticaria is a manifestation of a transfusion reaction when it occurs during a blood transfusion and is preventable by premedicating the client with an antihistamine

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A child with ADHD is prescribed methylphenidate. When should the mother give it?
questions.rationale: Methylphenidate is a CNS stimulant given before breakfast and before lunch. Afternoon or evening doses cause insomnia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1399 (PDF p. 1703)
questions.quote: Methylphenidate is a central nervous stimulant and should be taken before breakfast and before the noontime meal.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a gastric ulcer is on sucralfate 1 g four times daily. When should the client take it?
options: 1 hour before meals and at bedtime
questions.rationale: Sucralfate is taken 1 hour before meals and at bedtime so it can coat the ulcer before food and acid irritate it. It can cause constipation.
explanations: Too late to protect the ulcer.
Correct: before meals and at bedtime.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1403 (PDF p. 1709)
questions.quote: The medication should be scheduled for administration 1 hour before meals and at bedtime.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should a client with peptic ulcer disease take propantheline?
questions.rationale: Propantheline is an anticholinergic that decreases GI secretions and is given 30 minutes before meals.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1409 (PDF p. 1715)
questions.quote: It should be administered 30 minutes before meals.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After mastectomy, a client's tumor is estrogen receptor-positive. Which follow-up treatment is commonly prescribed?
questions.rationale: Tamoxifen competes with estrogen for binding sites in breast tissue and is commonly given for years after surgery for ER-positive tumors. Estrogen would stimulate the tumor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1416 (PDF p. 1722)
questions.quote: A common treatment for women with estrogen receptor–positive breast tumors is follow-up treatment with tamoxifen.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client takes donepezil hydrochloride. Which condition does the nurse expect the client to have?
questions.rationale: Donepezil raises acetylcholine levels and is used for mild to moderate Alzheimer's-type dementia. It slows disease progression.
explanations: Correct: a cholinergic agent for dementia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1417 (PDF p. 1723)
questions.quote: Donepezil hydrochloride is a cholinergic agent that is used in the treatment of mild to moderate dementia of the Alzheimer’s type.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Sertraline is prescribed for a client with depression. Which finding should make the nurse consult the prescriber first?
questions.rationale: Sertraline with an MAOI can cause serious, possibly fatal reactions. An MAOI must be stopped at least 14 days before sertraline, and vice versa.
explanations: Correct: SSRI plus MAOI is dangerous.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1422 (PDF p. 1728)
questions.quote: MAOIs should be stopped at least 14 days before sertraline therapy.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Tonio, 58, a farmer, has sputum-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. He is enrolled in the TB-DOTS program at the rural health unit, and his regimen includes streptomycin.
questions.stem: Which test result would indicate a TOXIC effect of streptomycin?
questions.rationale: Streptomycin is nephrotoxic, so BUN and creatinine are monitored. Vision testing is for ethambutol, and liver enzymes for isoniazid.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1425 (PDF p. 1734)
questions.quote: BUN and creatinine are measured during therapy with streptomycin because the medication is nephrotoxic.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Tonio, 58, a farmer, has sputum-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. He is enrolled in the TB-DOTS program at the rural health unit, and his regimen includes streptomycin.
questions.stem: Mang Tonio's regimen also includes ethambutol. Which test should the nurse expect to be done during therapy?
questions.rationale: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, so vision testing is done. Isoniazid requires liver monitoring, and streptomycin requires kidney monitoring.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1425 (PDF p. 1734)
questions.quote: Vision testing is done during treatment with ethambutol.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with multiple sclerosis is taking baclofen. Which finding shows a therapeutic response?
options: Full range of motion in all limbs
questions.rationale: Baclofen is a skeletal muscle relaxant that acts on the spinal cord to reduce the frequency and strength of muscle spasms.
explanations: It relaxes muscles rather than increasing tone.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1428 (PDF p. 1737)
questions.quote: acts at the spinal cord level to decrease the frequency and amplitude of muscle spasms
